fields.sections.0.h: Background of Shutdown Notice and Legal Pressure
fields.sections.1.h: Operator's Thanks and Commitment to Response
fields.sections.2.h: Scope of Technical Materials Provided by the Site
fields.sections.3.h: Implications for Development Ecosystem Signaled by Operational Shutdown
fields.sections.0.ko: The operator of a site that has provided unofficial developer reference materials received an official notice from Arm's legal team. Arm stated it will take legal action if the site is not shut down by December 4, 2026. This is not merely a request but a final ultimatum with legal force.
fields.sections.1.ko: The operator expressed gratitude to developers who have used this site for many years, as well as to users including Arm's internal personnel. While acknowledging the site's broad value, the operator announced plans to seek alternative solutions to maintain the functionality of bookmarks and links in order not to succumb to legal reality.
fields.sections.2.ko: The site facing shutdown has provided reference documentation on the AArch64 instruction set (ISA) and system registers defined in the Armv8-A and Armv9-A architectures. It was designed to allow developers to access technical information necessary for Arm processor development through search functionality and manual browsing.
fields.sections.3.ko: The elimination of unofficial but developer-friendly reference materials reveals Arm's intent to strengthen control over technical information. This could deepen the structure in which the open-source community and individual developers become more dependent on hardware platforms. Simultaneously, it means the disappearance of alternatives for information access outside official channels within the Arm ecosystem.
fields.caveat: Since the original text does not directly present Arm's official stated reasons for the shutdown, it is difficult to pinpoint the exact legal grounds such as copyright infringement or trademark protection.
